description: Legacy SlateDB run-catalog markers carry a start-date segment: runs/_index/by-start/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<ulid> (5 NUL-separated segments, date from RunId::key_segments()). Upstream v0.342 parse_run_catalog_key initially accepted only the 4-segment canonical form and its import tests seed only that synthetic layout via a #[cfg(test)] helper — real production data failed the fail-closed SQLite run-history activation at boot. Any future SlateDB key parser must be tested against the REAL writer layout (Record/Repository key_for_id + key_segments), not a hand-written canonical form.
resolution: Accept both layouts in the parser (31809f2ad): date segment validated strictly as chrono NaiveDate %Y-%m-%d, run id stays the final segment, everything else rejects; run_catalog_key_legacy test helper reproduces the writer layout byte-exactly; regression test proves date-prefixed markers import and count. Deployed activation completed on real data (75 runs / 42163 events).

description: fabro-3fe4 reopen (runs 01M25K41V4NE, 01M25R832HP): making the live reducer strictly apply the shared lifecycle table stranded injected event sequences (submitted + worker-shaped run.starting, RunRunnable suppressed by the scheduling guard) at Submitted, so fabro rm no longer saw terminal runs as completed and failed dogfood-gate. Lesson: when two reducers share one strict table, any per-reducer guard (RunRunnable suppression) must be paired with the shared fast-forward path, or live/durable status drift breaks downstream terminality predicates like requires_force_to_delete.
resolution: Shared helper fabro_types::historic_skipped_statuses consumed by BOTH live_lifecycle_status (server.rs) and RunProjectionReducer (run_state.rs); rm completed-run tests pass on final tree.

name: sqlite-busy-classification-and-wal-test-pools
description: SQLite BUSY resilience in fabro-store run-event writes (fabro-3ef7): sqlx surfaces the EXTENDED error code via DatabaseError::code() (e.g. 517 SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT), so busy classification must mask to the primary code (code & 0xff == 5) plus a 'database is locked' message fallback; and file-backed test pools must set journal_mode(Wal) to mirror the canonical fabro-db connect policy — rollback-journal test pools deadlocked forever (not code-5) when two same-process pools held overlapping write transactions, silently failing to reproduce the production incident.

name: sqlx-migrate-rerun-if-changed
description: Crates embedding sqlx::migrate! need a build.rs emitting cargo:rerun-if-changed=migrations (and =build.rs); cargo fingerprints do not reliably invalidate on migration file add/remove under local-target and docker-volume caches, shipping a stale MIGRATOR (fabro-bc9b). Pair with a unit test asserting max(MIGRATOR versions) equals max version parsed from the on-disk migrations dir via CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR, and log the newest embedded version at migrate() startup.

Whenever a migration file is added on a branch switch or cache reuse and behavior says 'column/migration missing': suspect the embedded MIGRATOR, not the DB. Diagnosis: query _sqlx_migrations (with -wal!) for the newest version. Mitigations: touch lib/foundation/fabro-db/src/lib.rs before just up after migration changes (until fabro-db gains rerun-if-changed in build.rs, filed as seed); cargo clean -p fabro-db for local test binaries. Deep lesson: /health + one API roundtrip is not deploy verification — the new automations smoke probe exists because the broken surface had no probe.
resolution: Smoke probe landed (authenticated automations check, live-proofed red on the broken deploy); build.rs hardening filed as P1 seed; deploy-watch-5 verifies the volume-cache rebuild.

description: Fail-closed SQLite run-history activation is version-sensitive: it replays all run events with the CURRENT projection code and compares against stored terminal rows, so any projection-semantics change (PR #240 quota Failed->Blocked reclassification on 2026-09-18) bricks startup for rows written by older binaries. CI never sees it (fresh DBs). Mitigation pattern that worked: copy prod DB (checkpoint WAL first — cp of the main file alone silently loses un-checkpointed writes), patch rows to the new projection (status column + summary_json lifecycle.status), validate in an isolated container (--network none, dummy SESSION_SECRET, prod settings.toml) until 'Activated SQLite run history' passes, then stop container + backup + patch + start on prod. Era-tolerance precedents live in run_summary_store.rs verify_run_json_field (workflow_version_id 2026-09-05, usage-rename 2026-09-15); seed fabro-eec6 owns the durable fix decision.
resolution: Mitigated 2026-09-18: 4 affected prod rows patched to the new projection (Blocked/quota_rate_limit) after isolated-container validation on a prod DB snapshot; prod healthy again on 0.360.0-nightly.0-15c046bd1. Durable fix (re-projection migration vs era-tolerance vs gate fixture) tracked in seed fabro-eec6.

description: Run-history activation crash-loop diagnosis recipe (2026-09-15, netcup-5): nightly crash-loop with exit 1 + 'stored run summary ... inconsistent field summary_json' means schema-era divergence between stored rows and the replayed projection. Reproduce offline: scp the fabro-storage volume, patch diag_replay_real_run_and_diff_summary_json to loop SELECT id FROM runs (or generalize to FABRO_DIAG_RUN), run FABRO_DIAG_DB=<copy> cargo nextest run -p fabro-store diag_replay_real_run — it prints every divergent JSON pointer per run. Cost equality check across rows proves whether a verify strip masks real drift. Full E2E before release: copy the whole /storage volume, run target/debug/fabro server start with FABRO_STORAGE_DIR/FABRO_HOME/FABRO_CONFIG pointing at the copy and SESSION_SECRET from gopass — install mode means FABRO_CONFIG did not resolve.
resolution: fix efa4a493f: era-gated billing/usage strip in verify_run_json_field + flat billing event normalizers in fork_legacy_read + decode lift; validated 38 runs / 21034 events against prod copy and live on netcup-5 (image 0.357.0-nightly.0-efa4a493f)

content: The runs table stores only repository_name, an owner/repository label derived via RepositoryRef::from_origin_and_source from the run spec git origin + source_directory. Any repository scoping key must be derived the same way (run_repository_label in lib/apps/fabro-cli/src/commands/run/runner.rs); runs without a git origin must stay unscoped, never filtered on the directory-basename fallback, or local runs would filter themselves out.
